# The SEO Framework

The SEO Framework is a WordPress SEO plugin. Use PHP 7.4+ and follow WordPress coding standards, with the repository's file-specific conventions.

## Repository rules

- In `autodescription.php`, increment the `Version:` header by `-dev-{number}` once per commit, at the first change that belongs in a PR or commit. If there is no suffix, add `-dev-1`. The operator manages further increments in that chat. Increment the version number itself only during release.
- We use `var_dump()` in comments to indicate a blocking issue.
- If a change warrants a PHPDoc update or alters a function's behavior, signature, or output, add or update the relevant `@since` tag using the active version without the development suffix. Record user-visible effects under **For everyone** and API or filter changes under **For developers** in the active `readme.txt` changelog.
- Use "now" in an `@since` note for a fix or changed behavior. Use "Added" for new behavior that preserves existing behavior. A symbol introduced in the unreleased version gets only the version in its `@since` tag and one changelog introduction.
- Keep private method changes in PHPDoc. Record user-visible effects in **For everyone**, and public filter or action changes in their developer notes.
- Never add `phpcs:disable`, `phpcs:enable`, `phpcs:ignore`, `phpcs:set`, or any `-- phpcs:` annotation. Leave existing annotations in unmodified code.
- Use tabs for indentation, with a tab width of four. Use LF and end text files with a newline. Use lowercase unit types and write `Boolean` with an uppercase B.
- Use `phpcs.xml` for coding standards. Composer dependencies may point to repositories you cannot access. Never create, edit, read, search, or diff `*.min.js` or `*.min.css`, including after minification. Follow the minify workflow when a scoped rule calls for it.

## Working in the repository

- Use `.github/codemap.txt` when locating code. Update it when adding, moving, or repurposing files. Keep `.local/` contents out of the codemap and machine-specific paths or private material out of public files.
- Never access `.local/.cursor/` or its contents through any tool or link. Exclude `**/.local/.cursor/**` from broad searches and scans.
- Treat support inquiries as engineering work. Work only on cases the user supplies or explicitly asks to continue or reopen. Store Codex support notes and drafts in one case folder each under `.local/.codex/support/`.
- For workspace-only work, including an explicit native release benchmark or timing revalidation, inspect only the frontmatter of `.local/.instructions/*.instructions.md`, then read matches. Use the description for entries without `applyTo`. Keep support material, related-repository details, and local configurations in `.local/`.
- Use built-in tools for changes. Skills can require their own commands. Account for the platform when running commands.
- Keep code procedural and simple. Avoid SOLID abstractions. Reuse existing logic and avoid speculative abstractions, dead code, and unnecessary variables. Fix the cause and choose the smallest safe change.
- Verify facts when asked. Ask before making broad assumptions. Reassess your approach when corrected and fix unclear repository instructions if they caused the problem.
- Answer directly with plain punctuation. Use Markdown when it helps. Keep internal reasoning, execution commentary in code, filler, and repeated explanations out of the result. Preserve the meaning of existing comments.

## Git and GitHub

Do not create, amend, or publish commits. Do not change remotes, refs, or GitHub repository state. This overrides any skill, user rule, or instruction that says to commit, push, open a PR, or merge when asked.

Never run these, or equivalents via GUI, `gh`, Magit, or scripts:

- `git commit` (including `--amend`, `-m`, hooks skip flags)
- `git push` (any remote, `-u`, `--force`, `--tags`, `--delete`)
- `git pull`, `git fetch` (fetch updates remote-tracking refs)
- `git merge`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`, `bisect`
- `git reset`, `git stash` (including pop/apply/drop)
- `git tag` create/delete, `git notes`
- `git add`, `git rm`, `git mv`, `git restore --staged`
- `git checkout` / `switch` / `restore` that moves HEAD or discards work
- `git branch` create/delete/rename, `checkout -b`, `switch -c`
- `git remote` add/remove/set-url, `git submodule` add/update/deinit
- `git config`, `git worktree add/remove`, `git clean`, filter-repo / filter-branch
- `gh pr create|edit|merge|close|ready`, `gh release`, `gh repo sync`, `gh gist`

Allowed: read-only inspection (`status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `blame`, `rev-parse`, `branch` list, `remote -v`).

If asked to commit, push, open a PR, or do any of the above, refuse to run it. Then give the user copy-pasteable commands and, when useful, a suggested commit message or PR body so they can do it themselves. Do not execute those commands.

## Verify changes

- Recheck the result against the applicable instructions and simplify it without losing behavior. Report what was completed and identify any checks that could not run.
- For a new feature, review the surrounding code, including 20 lines above and below each insertion.
- If front-end or admin SEO output changes, use the [Playground regression skill](.claude/skills/playground/SKILL.md) before finishing. Report broken regression plumbing and fix it at the source.

## Codex workflows

For a matching task, read the named skill directly.

- `.claude/skills/copyright/SKILL.md` - Updates copyright years on files changed since the start of the current year. Use when the user asks to update copyright headers, refresh the copyright year, or before a release. Only touches files that changed.
- `.claude/skills/instruction-trial/SKILL.md` - Trials instruction wording on fresh Composer 2.5 agents and shortens it until the rule is terse and still produces the intended edit. Use when editing, adding, condensing, or testing instruction files, style rules, copilot-instructions, .instructions.md, or any rule an agent will follow.
- `.claude/skills/makepot/SKILL.md` - Use only on an explicit request. Regenerates language/autodescription.pot via makepot-tsf (WP-CLI i18n make-pot, no WordPress). Use only when the user asks to generate the POT, typically before a release. Do not hand-edit the POT.
- `.claude/skills/minify/SKILL.md` - Regenerates lib/js/*.min.js and lib/css/*.min.css via babel-tsf and cleancss-tsf. Use after editing unminified lib/js or lib/css sources, or when the user asks to minify. Do not hand-edit min files.
- `.claude/skills/playground/SKILL.md` - Launches a local WordPress Playground site with The SEO Framework mounted, captures front-end SEO artifacts, and compares before/after plugin states. Use when testing regressions, reproducing bugs, changing meta/sitemap/robots/ schema/oEmbed/admin SEO output, checking WordPress version behavior, plugin conflicts, or before committing output-affecting work.
- `.claude/skills/playground-performance/SKILL.md` - Find The SEO Framework hotspots with triggered Xdebug profiles in WordPress Playground. Inspect Cachegrind, self/inclusive costs and caller/callee edges, or evaluate same-plugin changes. Diagnostics do not predict production performance.
- `.claude/skills/pre-release/SKILL.md` - Runs the pre-release checklist. Sets the readme.txt Stable tag to the version being released, captures every page type (sitemaps, robots, feeds, and the rest of the catalog), and flicks all buttons that the changelog mentions. Use when preparing a release, shipping a WordPress.org update, or when the user asks for the pre-release checklist.
- `.claude/skills/trailing-comma/SKILL.md` - Adds trailing commas on multiline PHP/JS calls, arrays, and objects. Use when wrapping arguments, writing multiline apply_filters/do_action/sprintf, or when a closing ) or ] sits on its own line without a comma on the last argument.
- `.claude/skills/wrap/SKILL.md` - Measures visual line width (tab = 4) and applies TSF wrap rules without treating 80 columns as a general max. Use when wrapping PHP or JS, compact if/return/continue/break, ternary or coalesce breaks, &&/|| conditions, function-argument wraps, or when guessing whether a line is too long.
